/-!
# Conjecture 8.25

by A. V. Kuznetsov

Does there exist an algorithm which recognizes by an identity whether it defines a
variety of groups that has at most countably many subvarieties?

An identity (law) is a word $w$ in the free group on the countably many variables
$x_0, x_1, \dots$; a group $G$ satisfies the identity $w = 1$ if $w$ evaluates to $1$
under every substitution of elements of $G$ for the variables. A variety of groups is
the class of all groups satisfying each identity in some set of identities, and the
variety defined by $w$ is the class of all groups satisfying $w = 1$. A subvariety of a
variety $\mathfrak{V}$ is a variety contained in $\mathfrak{V}$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
def SatisfiesLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, φ w = 1
blocks.docstring:
A group `G` satisfies the identity (law) `w = 1`, where `w` is a word in the free group
on the countably many variables `x₀, x₁, …`, if `w` evaluates to `1` under every substitution
of elements of `G` for the variables, i.e. under every homomorphism `FreeGroup ℕ →* G`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FreeGroup.lift / MonoidHom evaluation (used in the definition); Mathlib.ModelTheory has languages for rings and fields but no group language or equational theories.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.25».SatisfiesLaw
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of a group satisfying a law/identity w = 1 (∀ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, φ w = 1).

blocks.code: abbrev GroupClass : Type 1 := ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop
blocks.docstring:
A class of groups, i.e. a property of groups. Groups are taken in the universe `Type`; since
every variety is determined by its relatively free group of countable rank, which is countable,
this does not change the collection of subvarieties of a variety.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No class-of-groups notion in Mathlib; bare Pi type would be less readable.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.25».GroupClass
justification.why_needed: Type alias `∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop` for a class of groups, so varieties and their subvarieties can be collected in a `Set` and counted.

def varietyOf (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : GroupClass :=

blocks.docstring:

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing; Mathlib has no varieties of groups (only algebraic varieties).
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.25».varietyOf
justification.why_needed: The variety defined by a set of identities: the class of all groups satisfying each of them. Not in Mathlib.

blocks.code:
def IsVariety (𝒱 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), 𝒱 = varietyOf S
blocks.docstring:
A class of groups is a variety if it is the class of all groups satisfying each
identity in some set of identities.

justification.name: Kourovka.«8.25».IsVariety
justification.why_needed: A class of groups is a variety iff it is `varietyOf S` for some set of laws S (Neumann's definition; equivalent to Birkhoff's HSP characterisation).

blocks.name: IsVariety
blocks.text:
/-- A class of groups is a variety if it is the class of all groups satisfying each
identity in some set of identities. -/
def IsVariety (𝒱 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), 𝒱 = varietyOf S

blocks.code:
def subvarieties (𝒱 : GroupClass) : Set GroupClass :=
  {𝒲 | IsVariety 𝒲 ∧ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝒲 G → 𝒱 G}
blocks.docstring: The subvarieties of a class of groups `𝒱`: the varieties of groups contained in `𝒱`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Alternative: the set of fully invariant subgroups of `FreeGroup ℕ` containing w (Subgroup + Subgroup.map under all endomorphisms); rejected in favour of the literal class-of-groups reading, though it gives the same cardinality.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.25».subvarieties
justification.why_needed: The set of varieties contained in a given class, whose countability is the property to be decided.

theorem satisfiesLaw_commutator_iff (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    SatisfiesLaw G ⁅FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of 1⁆ ↔ IsMulCommutative G := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨⟨fun a b => ?_⟩⟩
    have := h (FreeGroup.lift fun n : ℕ => if n = 0 then a else b)
    rwa [map_commutatorElement, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm, FreeGroup.lift_apply_of,
      FreeGroup.lift_apply_of, if_pos rfl, if_neg one_ne_zero] at this
  · rintro ⟨⟨h⟩⟩ φ
    rw [map_commutatorElement, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm]
    exact h _ _

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no decidability question: 'an identity' is one group word w (element of the free group of countable rank, an encodable type, so 'algorithm' is ComputablePred/decidability of the predicate on w); 'the variety it defines' is the class of all groups satisfying the law w = 1 (equivalently its fully invariant verbal subgroup / set of all laws it implies); 'subvarieties' are varieties contained in it (which are determined by their sets of laws, so cardinality is well-defined); 'at most countably many' means cardinality ≤ ℵ₀ (finite or countably infinite); answer(True) means such an algorithm exists.
claims.reviewer_why: c03 defines a variety literally as in the source (the class of all groups satisfying a set of identities), the variety defined by w as varietyOf {w}, and subvarieties as varieties contained in it; 'at most countably many' is Set.Countable (≤ ℵ₀, finite allowed); 'algorithm' is ComputablePred on the identity given as a word List (ℕ × Bool) (Primcodable) mapped by FreeGroup.mk into the countable-rank free group — the predicate factors through FreeGroup.mk and word reduction is computable, so this is equivalent to decidability on free-group elements; answer(True) ↔ algorithm exists. Restriction of group classes to universe Type does not change the lattice of subvarieties (varieties are determined by their laws, witnessed in countable groups). Edits: added AMS 8 (varieties) and generalised one test to Type*. c01 is an equally faithful near-duplicate with fewer API tests; c02/c06 (consequence-closed law sets containing w) and c04/c05/c07/c08 (fully invariant subgroups of F_∞ containing w) are also faithful but one correspondence-theorem removed from the wording (c06 additionally introduces a global Primcodable (FreeGroup α) instance that belongs in FormalConjecturesForMathlib rather than a problem file).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.25

by A. V. Kuznetsov

Does there exist an algorithm which recognizes by an identity whether it defines a
variety of groups that has at most countably many subvarieties?

An identity (law) is a word $w$ in the free group on the countably many variables

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

namespace Kourovka.«8.25»

/-- A group `G` satisfies the identity (law) `w = 1`, where `w` is a word in the free group
on the countably many variables `x₀, x₁, …`, if `w` evaluates to `1` under every substitution
of elements of `G` for the variables, i.e. under every homomorphism `FreeGroup ℕ →* G`. -/
def SatisfiesLaw (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : FreeGroup ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, φ w = 1

/-- A class of groups, i.e. a property of groups. Groups are taken in the universe `Type`; since
every variety is determined by its relatively free group of countable rank, which is countable,
this does not change the collection of subvarieties of a variety. -/
abbrev GroupClass : Type 1 := ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop

/-- The variety of groups defined by a set `S` of identities: the class of all groups
satisfying every identity `w = 1` with `w ∈ S`. -/
def varietyOf (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : GroupClass :=
  fun G _ => ∀ w ∈ S, SatisfiesLaw G w

/-- A class of groups is a variety if it is the class of all groups satisfying each
identity in some set of identities. -/
def IsVariety (𝒱 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ), 𝒱 = varietyOf S

/-- The subvarieties of a class of groups `𝒱`: the varieties of groups contained in `𝒱`. -/
def subvarieties (𝒱 : GroupClass) : Set GroupClass :=
  {𝒲 | IsVariety 𝒲 ∧ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝒲 G → 𝒱 G}

/--
Does there exist an algorithm which recognizes by an identity whether it defines a
variety of groups that has at most countably many subvarieties?

An identity is given to the algorithm as a word `l : List (ℕ × Bool)` in the variables
`x₀, x₁, …` and their inverses, representing the element `FreeGroup.mk l` of the free group
of countable rank. The variety it defines is the class of all groups `G` satisfying
`FreeGroup.mk l = 1`, and the question asks whether the set of its subvarieties is
countable (finite or countably infinite) for the given identity, decided by an
algorithm, i.e. whether this predicate on words is a `ComputablePred`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.25» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ComputablePred fun l : List (ℕ × Bool) =>
      (subvarieties (varietyOf {FreeGroup.mk l})).Countable := by
  sorry

/-- Every group satisfies the trivial identity `1 = 1`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem satisfiesLaw_one (G : Type*) [Group G] : SatisfiesLaw G 1 :=
  fun φ => map_one φ

/-- The class of groups defined by a set of identities is a variety. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isVariety_varietyOf (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : IsVariety (varietyOf S) :=
  ⟨S, rfl⟩

/-- The variety defined by the empty set of identities is the class of all groups. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem varietyOf_empty (G : Type) [Group G] : varietyOf ∅ G :=
  fun _ h => h.elim

/-- Every variety is a subvariety of itself. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem mem_subvarieties_self (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) :
    varietyOf S ∈ subvarieties (varietyOf S) :=
  ⟨isVariety_varietyOf S, fun _ _ h => h⟩

/-- A group satisfies the identity `[x₀, x₁] = 1` if and only if it is commutative. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem satisfiesLaw_commutator_iff (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    SatisfiesLaw G ⁅FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of 1⁆ ↔ IsMulCommutative G := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨⟨fun a b => ?_⟩⟩
    have := h (FreeGroup.lift fun n : ℕ => if n = 0 then a else b)
    rwa [map_commutatorElement, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm, FreeGroup.lift_apply_of,
      FreeGroup.lift_apply_of, if_pos rfl, if_neg one_ne_zero] at this
  · rintro ⟨⟨h⟩⟩ φ
    rw [map_commutatorElement, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm]
    exact h _ _

end Kourovka.«8.25»

items: 'Algorithm' is modelled as `ComputablePred` (Mathlib's decidable-by-a-computable-function notion). Since Mathlib has no `Primcodable (FreeGroup ℕ)`, the identity is fed to the algorithm as a word `l : List (ℕ × Bool)` in the variables x₀, x₁, … and their inverses, standing for `FreeGroup.mk l`. Every element of the free group of countable rank is of this form and the predicate factors through `FreeGroup.mk`, so decidability on words is exactly decidability on identities (reduction of words is computable, so allowing unreduced words changes nothing).

'Identity' = a single element of `FreeGroup ℕ` (free group of countable rank), i.e. a law w = 1; an identity u = v is equivalent to uv⁻¹ = 1. A group satisfies it iff every homomorphism `FreeGroup ℕ →* G` kills w (`SatisfiesLaw`).

'Variety of groups' is defined equationally (H. Neumann's definition): a class of groups equal to the class of all groups satisfying some set of laws (`IsVariety`). By Birkhoff's theorem this coincides with classes closed under subgroups, quotients and direct products.
'Subvarieties' are the varieties contained (pointwise) in the given variety, collected as a `Set GroupClass` (in `Type 1`); 'at most countably many' is `Set.Countable` (finite or countably infinite).

Classes of groups are restricted to groups in universe `Type` (`GroupClass := ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop`), as is standard in this repository. This does not change the count: subvarieties are in bijection with fully invariant subgroups V of `FreeGroup ℕ` containing w, and distinct such V are separated by the countable (hence `Type`-level) relatively free groups `FreeGroup ℕ ⧸ V`, so the lattice of subvarieties of `Type`-groups is the usual one. An equivalent formulation would count fully invariant subgroups of `FreeGroup ℕ` containing w; the class-of-groups formulation was chosen because it follows the informal definitions literally.
The trivial identity (empty word) defines the variety of all groups, which has 2^ℵ₀ subvarieties, so the predicate is false there; no degenerate boundary case makes the statement trivial.
AMS tags 3 (logic/computability) and 20 (group theory); test lemmas are tagged AMS 20.

reviewer_notes: Single-slot problem; all eight candidates formalized it and compiled. No candidate omitted the slot. The only modelling choices are (a) input encoding of the identity — all but c06 use words List (ℕ × Bool) via FreeGroup.mk, which is computably equivalent to reduced words / FreeGroup ℕ; (b) how to count subvarieties — as equational classes of groups in Type (c01, c03), as consequence-closed sets of laws (c02, c06), or as fully invariant subgroups of F_∞ (c04, c05, c07, c08). All three are in bijection with the subvarieties of var(w) (for (b)/(c) via the standard Galois correspondence / the fact that fully invariant subgroups of the countably-infinite-rank free group are verbal), so all are faithful; the shipped file uses the most direct one. Universe restriction to `Type` for classes of groups follows repository convention (Kourovka 1.40) and is harmless here since a variety is determined by its countable relatively free group. Final file compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.
